title: Career Roadmap · Lab Technician
summary: A Medical Lab Technician collects and processes samples, performs routine diagnostic tests, operates laboratory equipment and records results to support doctors in diagnosing and monitoring diseases.

facts.Current degree: Diploma in Medical Laboratory Technology (DMLT) or an accepted laboratory-science qualification

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Science with Biology; Chemistry and Physics are important for many programmes.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, English and basic mathematics.

blocks.label: Entrance/admission
blocks.text: State counselling, entrance examination or merit-based admission, depending on the institution.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Human anatomy, microbiology, blood testing, microscopy and laboratory safety.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Accuracy, hygiene, observation, confidentiality and careful recordkeeping.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Eligibility, course duration and permitted professional duties vary by programme and applicable regulations. Confirm current requirements before admission.

items.text: DMLT / Diploma in Medical Laboratory Technology → Entry-level medical laboratory technician roles, subject to employer and regulatory requirements.
B.Sc. Medical Laboratory Technology / Medical Laboratory Science → Broader laboratory roles and further-study opportunities.
B.Sc. Medical Microbiology / Biochemistry → Laboratory pathways where the employer accepts the qualification.
Relevant postgraduate study → Advanced laboratory science, research or specialist roles, depending on eligibility.
Radiology / Optometry diplomas → Separate healthcare pathways; these are not substitutes for laboratory technology qualifications.
